entries.note: The central claim is qualified by 'I don’t think'; the supporting figures are separately checkable.

entries.test: Public utility capacity and interconnection records would show whether sufficient power was available to operate the cited capacity at publication.
entries.note: The concession concerns construction status; the asserted power shortage is present-tense.
'A disaster' evaluates the estimated capacity rather than adding a factual claim.

entries.test: Public GPU deployment schedules, customer purchasing explanations and NVIDIA revenue records would test whether sustaining revenue depends entirely on purchases years ahead of use.
entries.note: 'Depends wholly' makes an unusually strong causal claim, but one open to contrary evidence.
'Feels like' presents a tentative allegation of a coverup, rather than a firm assertion or empty insult.

entries.test: Historical data center announcements, commissioned gigawatt facility records and OpenAI financial disclosures would test the claimed age, apparent absence and inability to pay bills.
entries.note: The inability to find a facility is a search qualification, not an unequivocal assertion that none exists.

entries.test: Public data center financing agreements and lender disclosures would show whether private credit lenders are funding these deals.
entries.note: The insult accompanies a concrete financing claim.

entries.test: Nebius financing disclosures and eventual commissioning of its contracted Meta capacity would test the financing account and refute the claim that the capacity will never materialize.
entries.note: The build-duration estimate is probabilistic, but 'it’s never happening' is a firm, undated forecast.
'This suggests' qualifies the central glut prediction as an inference rather than a firm expectation.

entries.test: Public operator financial statements, debt-service costs, customer losses and NVIDIA valuation and construction-demand analyses would test the asserted profitability and valuation relationships.
entries.note: The claim that debt makes all AI data centers unprofitable has a clear financial test despite the surrounding emphatic language.

entries.test: Public installation and commissioning records through 2029 would show when GPUs represented by NVIDIA’s 2025 and 2026 sales became operational, given the stated construction assumptions.
entries.note: 'Operationalize revenues' plainly refers to putting the corresponding purchased hardware into service.

entries.test: Public capacity, utilization, pricing and revenue disclosures for US data centers newly operating in 2025 would test the implied tens-of-billions revenue expectation and reported shortfall.
entries.note: This compares an explicitly hypothetical revenue calculation with existing reported revenue.

entries.test: Published hyperscaler employment policies, compensation criteria and production-development records would show the scope of mandatory AI use, token-based incentives and nontechnical contributions.
entries.note: 'Everybody' and the compensation linkage are substantive parts of the claim.

entries.test: Publicly documented internal AI projects, functionality assessments and development-versus-time-saved measurements would test the claimed outcomes of mandated use.
entries.note: The disparaging presentation still contains factual claims about functionality and net time savings.

entries.test: Public comparative studies of generated code, coding-standard compliance, review time and reviewer behavior would test the asserted causal chain.
entries.note: 'Guaranteeing' and the exclusive reviewer alternatives are stronger than a mere tendency.

entries.test: Public code audits, incident reports and staffing histories would test whether generated code and engineer departures degrade systems and alter incident prevention.
entries.note: The normalization replaces 'raising' with an unspecified effect and proposes 'lowering.' That repairs an apparent error instead of preserving the stated direction.

entries.test: A public incident postmortem would establish whether a major big-tech service suffered a prolonged failure caused by widespread AI coding and compounded by lost expertise.
entries.note: 'I am certain' is firm expectation; 'near future' supplies no definite deadline.
'Crisis after crisis' supplies no shared criterion for the predicted outcomes. The subscription figures are separately checkable.

entries.test: Public longitudinal studies of engineers relying almost exclusively on LLMs would test subsequent skill loss, required retraining and claimed dependence on model training limits.
entries.note: The normalization omits the specific limitation to the model’s last training run and makes 'only really used' more absolute.

entries.test: Public AI revenue disclosures and controlled workplace productivity studies would test the revenue and lack-of-benefit assertions, with large-scale studies addressing the tentative harm claim.
entries.note: The categorical absence of tangible productivity benefits is testable; 'seems' qualifies only the additional harm assertion.
